info.name: SmartOLT
info.description:
SmartOLT API

Machine-readable version (OpenAPI, for tools and AI assistants): https://www.smartolt.com/openapi.json

---

🔴 The API changed. Please read this page again.

Updated October 2026. Check your integration against these changes:

  • 🆕 Real-time events. Get ONU status changes, ONU changes, signal changes and PON outages when they occur. Use an event stream (SSE) or a webhook. You do not need to poll the API. See Real-time events below.
  • ⚡ Asynchronous calls for high-volume actions. Send async=1 to enable or disable ONUs, change CATV or change speed profiles. The request does not wait for the OLT. See Asynchronous calls below.
  • 📦 Bulk actions. One bulk call can contain up to 10,000 ONU IDs with async=1. Do not send one call for each ONU. See Recommended API usage below.
  • 🆕 ONU status history. Get how long an ONU was Online, LOS, Power fail or Offline, for up to 365 days. See Get ONU status history by ONU unique external ID.
  • 🆕 MAC addresses. Get the MAC addresses behind an ONU, or find the ONU of a MAC address. See Get ONU MAC addresses by ONU unique external ID and Search ONU by MAC address.

⚠️ If your system polls Get all ONUs statuses or Get all ONUs signals, change it to use real-time events.

---

How to call the API

  • Send each request to https://<your-subdomain>.smartolt.com/api/....
  • Send your API key in the X-Token header.
  • Every response has status. When status is false, read error for the message and error_code for the reason, when it is present. A call over the API call rate limit is the exception. See Limits.

Limits

API access is a privilege. Use it responsibly.

  • The default budget is 1,000 API calls per hour. For very large installations, we can review and extend the budget if the operational requirements justify it.
  • Asynchronous calls have their own budget, by default 5,000 calls per hour.
  • The default limit is 15 calls per second. If you send more, all your calls are blocked for 10 seconds.
  • Some endpoints have their own hourly limit. The description of the endpoint gives it.
  • When you are over the per-hour, per-10-minute or per-second limit, the API returns HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header. Wait that number of seconds before you call again.
  • The body of that 429 has response_code set to rate_limit_exceeded and the message in response. It also has violation_type (per_hour, per_10min or per_second) and retry_after, the same number of seconds.
  • When you are over the limit of one endpoint, the 429 has error and error_code, like other errors.
  • Each response has X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers. X-RateLimit-Reset is the number of seconds until the budget resets.

If you use the API too much, SmartOLT can limit your calls or revoke your API access.

Keep a local copy of your data and update it from events.

Add a random delay to scheduled requests. For example, do not send a request exactly every 5 minutes at fixed times. Add a small random delay to each call, so that many systems do not call the API at the same time.

Real-time events (new)

Receive changes as they happen. SmartOLT can now notify your integration when something changes: an ONU goes offline, its signal drops, a new ONU appears unconfigured, or a PON port fails. Use webhooks or the event stream instead of asking for the status of every ONU every few minutes.

  • Event stream (SSE): your system keeps one connection open, and the events arrive on it.
  • Webhook: SmartOLT sends each batch of events as an HTTPS POST to your URL. Set it up in General > API key > Edit > Webhook.

Event types: onu.status_changed, onu.authorized, onu.updated, onu.deleted, onu.signal_changed, onu.signal_reading, onu.rx1490_reading, pon.outage_started, pon.outage_ended, olt.outage_started, olt.outage_ended, olt.status_stale, olt.status_fresh, onu.unconfigured_detected. See the Real-time events folder.

Asynchronous calls (recommended for high-volume actions)

For high-volume actions, use asynchronous calls. Use them to enable ONUs, disable ONUs, change CATV or change speed profiles on many ONUs. Send async=1 with the request. SmartOLT checks the request, puts the work in a queue and returns immediately. The request does not wait for the OLT.

These endpoints accept async=1:

  • Single ONU: enable, disable, enable_catv, disable_catv, update_onu_speed_profiles
  • Multiple ONUs: bulk_enable, bulk_disable, bulk_enable_catv, bulk_disable_catv, bulk_update_speed_profiles

bulk_apply_configuration_preset and bulk_remove_configuration_preset are always asynchronous. They also use the asynchronous budget.

Why use asynchronous calls:

  • The request returns immediately. A normal request waits until the OLT finishes the command.
  • A bulk call accepts up to 10,000 ONU IDs with async=1, and only up to 50 ONU IDs without async=1.
  • Asynchronous calls use their own hourly budget, not the normal budget.
  • SmartOLT runs all actions for one ONU in the order it received them.

How to use asynchronous calls:

  1. Send the request with async=1.
  2. Read the queued field in the response. It shows which ONUs SmartOLT queued.
  3. Some minutes later, call check_bulk_task_status to see the result for each ONU. Do not call it in a tight loop. Each status check counts in the normal hourly budget.

Important: "queued": true means that SmartOLT accepted the action. It does not mean that the OLT did it. A request without async=1 can also return "queued": true when the ONU already has queued actions. Do not mark the action as done until check_bulk_task_status shows succeeded.

Recommended API usage

  • ONU statuses
    • Use the onu.status_changed real-time event.
    • If you cannot use events, call Get all ONUs statuses every 5-7 minutes, and store the response between calls.
  • ONU signal levels
    • Use the onu.signal_reading or onu.signal_changed real-time events for the 1310 value, and the onu.rx1490_reading event for the 1490 value.
    • Call Get all ONUs signals at start-up or after a resync event. If you cannot use events, call it every 15-30 minutes, and store the response between calls.
  • High-volume actions (enable, disable, CATV, speed profiles on many ONUs)
    • Use one bulk call with async=1 for up to 10,000 ONU IDs. Without async=1, a bulk call can only contain up to 50 ONU IDs.
    • Do not send one call for each ONU.

Important: Do not poll individual ONUs again and again when a bulk endpoint or a real-time event gives the same data. Your integration must store data, use reasonable polling intervals and use bulk calls. If your integration uses the API too much, SmartOLT can limit its calls to protect the platform for all users.

item.name: Real-time events
Get event stream URL

header.description: (Required) The API token

query.description: (String) The event types to get, separated by commas. Leave it empty to get only onu.status_changed. Known types: onu.status_changed, onu.unconfigured_detected, onu.authorized, onu.updated, onu.deleted, pon.outage_started, pon.outage_ended, olt.outage_started, olt.outage_ended, olt.status_stale, olt.status_fresh, onu.signal_changed, onu.signal_reading, onu.rx1490_reading

request.description:
Gets a URL for a live event stream (Server-Sent Events). Open the URL with any SSE client, for example EventSource or curl -N.

How to use it

  1. Call this endpoint. Select the event types with events.
  2. Open the returned url within expires_in seconds (15 minutes).
  3. Read the events. Each event has an id, an event (the event type) and a data line with the event body.
  4. The stream closes after about 1 hour. Then call this endpoint again and open the new URL. Send the last id you got in the Last-Event-ID header. You then get the events that you missed.

Control events

  • resync: you missed events. Load the current data again, for example with Get all ONUs statuses.
  • expired: the stream is closed. Get a new URL.
  • disabled: the stream is closed because the API key was disabled or changed. Get a new URL.
  • A : ping comment comes every 25 seconds to keep the connection open.

Limits

  • You can call this endpoint up to 60 times per hour.
  • Each account can have up to 15 open streams for API keys.

It returns a 400 error code when events contains an unknown event type.

It returns a 403 error code when the API key is not a client API key.

It returns a 503 error code when the event stream is not available. Use Get all ONUs statuses until it is available again.

item.name: Webhook delivery (sent by SmartOLT to your server)

header.description: The ID of the batch. A retry sends the same ID.
The time of the send, in Unix seconds.
v1, followed by the base64 HMAC-SHA256 signature.

request.description:
This item is documentation only. You do not send this request. SmartOLT sends it to your server.

How to set up a webhook

  1. Go to General > API key. Click Edit on your API key.
  2. In the Webhook panel, enter your HTTPS URL and select the events.
  3. Copy the Signing secret.
  4. Click Send test event. Your server gets a webhook.test event.

Your server must

  • Use HTTPS on port 443 or 8443, with a valid certificate and a public IP address.
  • Return an HTTP 2xx status within 15 seconds. Redirects count as failures.
  • Ignore a webhook-id that it already processed. A retry sends the same webhook-id and body.

Retries: after a failure, SmartOLT sends the batch again after 5 seconds, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours, 5 hours, and then every 10 hours. After 5 days of failures, SmartOLT disables the webhook and sends you an email. You can enable it again on the API key page.

Headers

  • webhook-id: the ID of the batch, for example msg_3f2a....
  • webhook-timestamp: the time of the send, in Unix seconds.
  • webhook-signature: v1, followed by the signature.

How to check the signature

  1. Remove the whsec_ prefix from your signing secret. Decode the rest from base64. This is the key.
  2. Make the text {webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}.
  3. Calculate HMAC-SHA256 of the text with the key. Encode the result in base64.
  4. Compare it with the value after v1,. If they are not equal, reject the request.

This follows theStandard Webhooksformat, so you can also use their libraries.

``` // PHP example $key = base64_decode(substr($secret, 6)); $signed = $_SERVER['HTTP_WEBHOOK_ID'] . '.' . $_SERVER['HTTP_WEBHOOK_TIMESTAMP'] . '.' . file_get_contents('php://input'); $expected = 'v1,' . base64_encode(hash_hmac('sha256', $signed, $key, true)); $valid = hash_equals($expected, $_SERVER['HTTP_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE']); ```

Example bodies for each event type are in the saved examples of this item.

item.description:
Get ONU, PON and OLT events in real time. You do not need to poll the API.

You can get the events in two ways:

- **Event stream (SSE)**: your system keeps one HTTP connection open, and the events arrive on it. See *Get event stream URL*.
- **Webhook**: SmartOLT sends each batch of events as an HTTPS POST to your URL. See *Webhook delivery*.

Both ways send the same event body:

```
{"type": "onu.status_changed", "timestamp": "2026-10-08T10:00:00Z", "data": {"onus": [ ... ]}}
```

ONU events put the rows in `data.onus`. PON events put the rows in `data.pons`. OLT events put the rows in `data.olts`. One batch has one event type and up to 1000 rows.

Event types:

- `onu.status_changed`: the ONU status changed (Online, LOS, Power fail, Offline).
- `onu.authorized`: an ONU was authorized.
- `onu.updated`: the configuration or details of an ONU changed. You get the full current ONU row.
- `onu.deleted`: an ONU was deleted.
- `onu.signal_changed`: the ONU signal moved to another band, or changed by 2 dB or more. `reading_at` is the time of the reading, in the time zone of your SmartOLT account.
- `onu.signal_reading`: each new ONU signal reading. It gives `rx1310`, the power that the OLT receives from the ONU (upstream). For the power that the ONU receives, see `onu.rx1490_reading`. `reading_at` is the time of the reading, in the time zone of your SmartOLT account.
- `onu.rx1490_reading`: each new reading of the power that the ONU receives from the OLT (downstream, 1490 nm, or 1577 nm on XG-PON and XGS-PON). The field is `rx1490` on all PON types. SmartOLT sends one event for each new reading that it stores for the ONU. A reading of -40 dBm or lower means no signal and is not sent. The rows have no `band` field. `reading_at` is the time of the reading, in the time zone of your SmartOLT account.
- `pon.outage_started`: a PON outage started. `olt_outage` is the ID of the OLT outage that the PON is part of, or `null`. A PON outage that starts before SmartOLT records the OLT outage has `null`.
- `pon.outage_ended`: a PON outage ended. `olt_outage` is the ID of the OLT outage that the PON is part of when SmartOLT writes the event, or `null`.
- `olt.outage_started`: all PONs with ONUs on an OLT went down at the same time, with cause `offline`. For example, the OLT rebooted. An OLT outage needs at least 2 PONs with ONUs. A PON outage with cause `los` or `power` does not start an OLT outage. SmartOLT does not start an OLT outage while it cannot reach the OLT. SmartOLT still sends `pon.outage_started` and `pon.outage_ended` for each PON. The row has `olt_id`, `olt_name`, `olt_outage` (the ID of the OLT outage), `pons` (the PONs in the outage, as `board/port`), `pon_count`, `onu_count` (the ONUs on these PONs) and `started_at` (when the first PON went down, in the time zone of your SmartOLT account).
- `olt.outage_ended`: an OLT outage ended. Every PON in the outage came back, or 15 minutes passed since the first PON came back. A PON that is still down after these 15 minutes stays in its own PON outage. The row has the same fields as `olt.outage_started`, and `ended_at`, in the time zone of your SmartOLT account. When the OLT is disabled during the outage, SmartOLT sends `olt.outage_ended` after the OLT is enabled again. When the OLT is deleted during the outage, SmartOLT does not send `olt.outage_ended`.
- `olt.status_stale`: SmartOLT has not read the ONU statuses of an OLT for 15 minutes, usually because the OLT is unreachable. The last ONU statuses of that OLT can be old. Get all ONUs statuses shows them as Unknown.
- `olt.status_fresh`: SmartOLT reads the ONU statuses of the OLT again.
- `onu.unconfigured_detected`: a new ONU appeared in the Unconfigured list of an OLT. Disabled ONUs are not sent. An ONU that leaves the list and comes back within 15 minutes is not sent again.

An API key that is limited to some PONs of an OLT, or to some zones, gets only its own PONs in the `pons` of an OLT outage, without `pon_count` and `onu_count`. When none of its PONs is in the OLT outage, the key does not get the event.

Only API keys that you create in SmartOLT can use events.

item.name: Get OLT uptime and environment temperature

header.description: (Required) The API token

request.description:
Gets the uptime, the environment temperature and the input voltage of one OLT, by OLT ID.

The voltage comes from the SmartOLT database. This endpoint does not read the voltage from the OLT.

**Fields**

- `uptime`: how long the OLT has been running since its last restart, as text. It is `N/A` when the OLT does not answer.
- `env_temp`: the environment temperature of the OLT, in degrees Celsius, as text with the unit (for example `38°C`). It is an empty string when the OLT does not answer.
- `color_class`: `text-danger` when `env_temp` is over the OLT temperature level "critical", `text-warning` when it is over the OLT temperature level "warning", and an empty string otherwise. Both levels are set in the OLT settings, on the Advanced tab. It is an empty string when the OLT does not answer.
- `voltage`: the last input voltage reading of the OLT, in volts (V), as a number. For an OLT with an AC input it is the AC voltage. It is `null` when the OLT does not report its input voltage, when the last reading is not a valid DC or AC input voltage, when the last reading is more than 30 minutes old, and when the OLT does not answer (`uptime` is `N/A`).
- `voltage_read_at`: the date and time of that reading, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in the time zone of your SmartOLT account. It is `null` when `voltage` is `null`.
- `power_state`: the power state of the OLT, from its voltage readings. The usual voltage is the voltage of the OLT on mains in the last 24 hours. It is `null` when `voltage` is `null`.
  - `normal`: the input voltage is at the usual voltage of the OLT. An OLT with an AC input is always `normal`.
  - `on_battery`: the input voltage dropped under the usual voltage of the OLT. The OLT is probably running on battery.
  - `battery_low`: the OLT is on battery and the input voltage is under 46 V and at least 3 V under its usual voltage. The battery is probably almost empty.

It returns a 400 error code when no OLT was found for the provided OLT ID (error code `specify_valid_olt_id`).

It returns a 403 error code when the OLT is outside the restriction group of your API key, and when the subscription of the OLT is not valid.

item.name: Get ONU types list

header.description: (Required) The API token

request.description:
Gets a list of all ONU types as defined in SmartOLT ONU Types section.   

Each ONU type consists of:

- unique ID
- name
- PON type (it can be "gpon" or "epon")
- capability (it can be "Bridging" or "Bridging/Routing")
- number of ethernet ports
- number of WiFi ports
- number of VoIP ports
- CATV
- if it allows custom ONU profiles (1 - it allows, 0 - it doesn't allow)
- band layout of the WiFi SSIDs: `wifi_radios`, `wifi_5g_first_slot` and `wifi_first_radio_band`, described below

**WiFi band fields**

SmartOLT puts the WiFi SSIDs of an ONU type into two groups, one per radio. The SSIDs before a boundary SSID form the first group. The boundary SSID and the SSIDs after it form the second group.

- `wifi_radios`: `null`, `1` or `2`.
  - `null`: no band layout is set. SmartOLT splits the SSIDs by their number: with 5 to 8 SSIDs the second group starts at SSID 5, with 9 or 10 at SSID 6, with 14 at SSID 8, with 16 at SSID 9. With any other number all SSIDs are in the first group.
  - `1`: single band. All SSIDs are on the 2.4 GHz radio.
  - `2`: dual band. The second group starts at `wifi_5g_first_slot`. When `wifi_5g_first_slot` is `null`, SmartOLT uses the split above; with 4 SSIDs the second group starts at SSID 3.
- `wifi_5g_first_slot`: the first SSID of the second group, from 2 to the number of SSIDs. It is `null` when `wifi_radios` is not `2`, or when SmartOLT uses the split by number.
- `wifi_first_radio_band`: `"5g"` when the first group is on the 5 GHz radio and the second group on the 2.4 GHz radio. It is `null` when the first group is on 2.4 GHz. It is `"5g"` only for an ONU type with at least 5 SSIDs and `wifi_radios` other than `1`. SmartOLT sets it for ONU types named like a device model that has its 5 GHz SSIDs first, for example Tenda HG9 or V-SOL V2802ACT. When `wifi_first_radio_band` is `"5g"`, `wifi_5g_first_slot` is the first 2.4 GHz SSID.

For an ONU that reports its WiFi radios over TR-069, SmartOLT uses the layout it reads from the ONU instead of these fields.

item.name: Get ONU types list by PON type

header.description: (Required) The API token

request.description:
Gets a list of ONU types by PON type (it can be "gpon" or "epon"), as defined in SmartOLT ONU Types section.   

Each ONU type consists of:

- unique ID
- name
- PON type (it can be "gpon" or "epon")
- capability (it can be "Bridging" or "Bridging/Routing")
- number of ethernet ports
- number of WiFi ports
- number of VoIP ports
- CATV
- if it allows custom ONU profiles (1 - it allows, 0 - it doesn't allow)
- band layout of the WiFi SSIDs: `wifi_radios`, `wifi_5g_first_slot` and `wifi_first_radio_band`, described below

**WiFi band fields**

SmartOLT puts the WiFi SSIDs of an ONU type into two groups, one per radio. The SSIDs before a boundary SSID form the first group. The boundary SSID and the SSIDs after it form the second group.

- `wifi_radios`: `null`, `1` or `2`.
  - `null`: no band layout is set. SmartOLT splits the SSIDs by their number: with 5 to 8 SSIDs the second group starts at SSID 5, with 9 or 10 at SSID 6, with 14 at SSID 8, with 16 at SSID 9. With any other number all SSIDs are in the first group.
  - `1`: single band. All SSIDs are on the 2.4 GHz radio.
  - `2`: dual band. The second group starts at `wifi_5g_first_slot`. When `wifi_5g_first_slot` is `null`, SmartOLT uses the split above; with 4 SSIDs the second group starts at SSID 3.
- `wifi_5g_first_slot`: the first SSID of the second group, from 2 to the number of SSIDs. It is `null` when `wifi_radios` is not `2`, or when SmartOLT uses the split by number.
- `wifi_first_radio_band`: `"5g"` when the first group is on the 5 GHz radio and the second group on the 2.4 GHz radio. It is `null` when the first group is on 2.4 GHz. It is `"5g"` only for an ONU type with at least 5 SSIDs and `wifi_radios` other than `1`. SmartOLT sets it for ONU types named like a device model that has its 5 GHz SSIDs first, for example Tenda HG9 or V-SOL V2802ACT. When `wifi_first_radio_band` is `"5g"`, `wifi_5g_first_slot` is the first 2.4 GHz SSID.

For an ONU that reports its WiFi radios over TR-069, SmartOLT uses the layout it reads from the ONU instead of these fields.

item.name: Add ONU type

header.description: (Required) The API token

formdata.description: (Required, String) ONU type
(Required, String) ONU type PON type. Allowed values: gpon, epon
(Required, Int) The number of ethernet ports. Allowed values: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 16, 24
(Required) (Int) The number of WiFi SSIDs. Allowed values: 0, 4, 8, 10
(Required, Int) The number of VoIP ports. Allowed values: 0, 1, 2
(Required, Int) 1 if it supports CATV, otherwise 0
(Required, Int) 1 if it allows custom profiles, otherwise 0
(Required, String) ONU type capability. Allowed values: Bridging/Routing, Bridging

(Int) Optional. 1 = single band, all SSIDs on 2.4 GHz. 2 = dual band, 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz. Needs `wifi_ssids_nr` 4, 8 or 10. Without it, SmartOLT splits the SSIDs by their number (see Get ONU types list).

(Int) Optional, only with `wifi_radios` 2. The first SSID of the second radio, from 2 to `wifi_ssids_nr`. Without it, the second radio starts at SSID 5 with 8 SSIDs, at SSID 6 with 10 SSIDs and at SSID 3 with 4 SSIDs.

request.description:
Adds a new ONU type.

A read-only API key cannot use this call. The response is HTTP 403 with `error_code` `forbidden` and the message `Readonly API Key doesn't have rights to make changes.`, and SmartOLT does not add the ONU type.

**WiFi bands**

`wifi_radios` and `wifi_5g_first_slot` set which radio each WiFi SSID uses. Get ONU types list describes the layout. The call cannot set which radio comes first: SmartOLT sets the 5 GHz first layout by itself when `name` matches a device model with its 5 GHz SSIDs first, for example `HG9` or `V2802ACT` (same letters, any case). For such a type `wifi_5g_first_slot` is the first 2.4 GHz SSID.

SmartOLT answers HTTP 400 and does not add the ONU type when:

- `wifi_ssids_nr` is not 0, 4, 8 or 10: `error_code` `incorrect_wifi_ssids_nr`.
- `wifi_radios` is set to a value other than 1 or 2: `error_code` `incorrect_wifi_radios`.
- `wifi_radios` is set and `wifi_ssids_nr` is 0: `error_code` `incorrect_wifi_radios`.
- `wifi_5g_first_slot` is set and `wifi_radios` is not set, or is 1: `error_code` `incorrect_wifi_5g_first_slot`.
- `wifi_5g_first_slot` is not a whole number from 2 to `wifi_ssids_nr`: `error_code` `incorrect_wifi_5g_first_slot`.

Update an existing splitter by its unique external ID. At least one field must be sent, otherwise the call fails with `nothing_to_update`.

**Selecting the Splitter.** The URL segment is the splitter's unique `external_id`. Alternatively post `odb_id` with the internal numeric ID - if both are provided, then the internal ID is used to select the splitter.

A read-only API key cannot use this call. The response is HTTP 403 with `error_code` `forbidden` and the message `Readonly API Key doesn't have rights to make changes.`, and SmartOLT does not change the splitter.

`error_code`: `specify_odb_id` (400, neither selector sent), `odb_does_not_exist` (400), 403 with `error_code` `forbidden` when the key has no access to the splitter's zone or the splitter itself, `nr_of_ports_below_used` (400), `nothing_to_update` (400), plus the same field-validation codes as Add Splitter.

Setting `external_id` to a value already used by another splitter fails with `external_id_not_unique` (400).

response.name: 200 - OK

item.name: Delete Splitter by unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

formdata.description: (Int) Internal numeric ID; takes precedence over the URL segment.

request.description:
Deletes a splitter.

**Selecting the splitter.** The URL segment is the `external_id` of the splitter. You can also post `odb_id` with the internal numeric ID. When the request has both, SmartOLT uses `odb_id`.

**What the delete removes.** The API has no confirmation step. SmartOLT deletes the splitter in one transaction with its cables, its fiber splices, its input links and its closed tickets.

SmartOLT checks the request in this order and stops at the first refusal. A refused request deletes nothing and changes nothing. The refusals are:

- the API key is read-only: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `Readonly API Key doesn't have rights to make changes.`
- the URL has no external ID and the request has no `odb_id`: HTTP 400, `error_code` `specify_odb_id`, message `Invalid parameters: Please specify the ODB external ID or the odb_id`.
- two or more splitters have this external ID: HTTP 409, `error_code` `ambiguous_external_id`, message `Multiple ODBs share the external ID <external_id>; use the odb_id parameter instead`.
- no splitter has this external ID or this `odb_id`: HTTP 400, `error_code` `odb_does_not_exist`, message `Invalid parameters: ODB does not exist`.
- the data access group of the API key does not include the zone of the splitter, or does not include the splitter itself: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `The API key does not have access to this ODB`.
- ONUs are assigned to the splitter: HTTP 409, `error_code` `odb_in_use`, message `This ODB is assigned to <count> ONU(s) and cannot be deleted`. `<count>` is the number of these ONUs.
- the splitter has open tickets: HTTP 409, `error_code` `odb_has_tickets`, message `This ODB has <count> open ticket(s) and cannot be deleted`. `<count>` is the number of open tickets.
- a fiber route starts or ends at the splitter: HTTP 409, `error_code` `odb_has_fiber_routes`, message `This ODB is the end of a fiber route and cannot be deleted`.
- the database does not save the delete: HTTP 500, `error_code` `odb_delete_failed`, message `The ODB could not be deleted`.

On success, `response` is `ODB <name> deleted successfully`.

response.name: 200 - OK
403 - Read-only API key
409 - ONUs assigned to the splitter
409 - Open tickets on the splitter
409 - Fiber route ends at the splitter

item.name: Add Distribution cabinet

header.description: (Required) The API token

urlencoded.description: (Required) (String) Required. Unique in its zone. SmartOLT saves at most 500 characters. An empty value returns HTTP 400 with `error_code` `specify_cabinet_name`.
(String) Zone name. It must name an existing zone; SmartOLT does not create zones here. A name that matches no zone returns HTTP 400 with `error_code` `zone_does_not_exist`.
(String) A number greater than -90 and less than 90. Another value returns HTTP 400 with `error_code` `incorrect_latitude`.
(String) A number from -180 to 180. Another value returns HTTP 400 with `error_code` `incorrect_longitude`.

(String) At most 191 characters, and not used by another distribution cabinet. This is the key that selects the cabinet on edit and delete. A longer value returns HTTP 400 with `error_code` `incorrect_external_id`; a used value returns HTTP 400 with `error_code` `external_id_not_unique`.
(String) SmartOLT saves at most 2000 characters.

request.description:
Adds a new distribution cabinet. Only `name` is required.

**Zone.** `zone` is the zone name, as returned by Get zones. When you leave out `zone` or send it empty, the cabinet has no zone. There is one exception: an API key whose data access group has exactly one zone puts the cabinet in that zone.

**Position.** The cabinet gets a position on the map only when the request has both `latitude` and `longitude` and they are not both 0. When the request has only one of them, or both are 0, SmartOLT saves the cabinet without a position and returns no error.

**Other fields.** SmartOLT removes the spaces at the start and the end of `name`, `external_id` and `note`. SmartOLT saves at most 500 characters of `name` and 2000 characters of `note`, and cuts a longer value. An empty `external_id` or `note` saves the cabinet without that field.

SmartOLT checks the request in this order and stops at the first refusal. A refused request creates nothing. The refusals are:

- the API key is read-only: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `Readonly API Key doesn't have rights to make changes.`
- `zone` contains a character other than a letter (a-z, A-Z), a digit, a space, an underscore, a dot or a dash: HTTP 400, `error_code` `incorrect_zone`, message `Invalid parameters: The zone can contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces, underscore, dot and the dash (-) character`.
- `zone` names a zone that is not in the data access group of the API key: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `The API key does not have access to this zone`.
- `zone` matches no zone name: HTTP 400, `error_code` `zone_does_not_exist`, message `Invalid parameters: Zone does not exist`. SmartOLT does not create the zone.
- `zone` is missing or empty, the API key has a data access group, and the group has two or more zones: HTTP 400, `error_code` `specify_zone`, message `Invalid parameters: Please specify a zone`.
- `name` is empty or contains only spaces: HTTP 400, `error_code` `specify_cabinet_name`, message `Invalid parameters: Please specify a name for the cabinet`.
- another distribution cabinet in the same zone has the same name: HTTP 400, `error_code` `cabinet_already_exists`, message `Invalid parameters: A cabinet with the same name already exists on this zone`. The comparison ignores letter case. When the cabinet has no zone, the name must be unique among the distribution cabinets that have no zone.
- `latitude` is not empty and is not a number greater than -90 and less than 90: HTTP 400, `error_code` `incorrect_latitude`, message `Invalid parameters: The Latitude is invalid`.
- `longitude` is not empty and is not a number from -180 to 180: HTTP 400, `error_code` `incorrect_longitude`, message `Invalid parameters: The Longitude is invalid`.
- `external_id` is longer than 191 characters: HTTP 400, `error_code` `incorrect_external_id`, message `Invalid parameters: The external ID is too long (maximum 191 characters)`.
- another distribution cabinet already has this `external_id`: HTTP 400, `error_code` `external_id_not_unique`, message `Invalid parameters: The external ID <external_id> is already used by another cabinet`. The comparison ignores letter case and trailing spaces.
- the database does not save the cabinet: HTTP 400, `error_code` `cabinet_add_failed`, message `Invalid parameters: The adding of the cabinet failed`.

On success, `response.id` is the ID of the new cabinet and `response.message` is `Distribution cabinet <name> added successfully`.

response.name: 200 - OK
400 - Name already used in the zone
400 - Zone does not exist
400 - External ID already used
403 - Read-only API key
403 - No access to the zone

(String) New note. SmartOLT saves at most 2000 characters. An empty value removes the note.

request.description:
Updates an existing distribution cabinet. Send only the fields you want to change. SmartOLT does not change the fields that the request leaves out.

**Selecting the distribution cabinet.** The URL segment is the unique `external_id` of the cabinet. The match ignores letter case. You can also post `cabinet_id` with the internal numeric ID. When the request has both, SmartOLT uses `cabinet_id`.

**Clearing a field.** An empty `zone` removes the cabinet from its zone; an API key whose data access group has exactly one zone puts the cabinet in that zone instead. An empty `external_id` removes the external ID; after that, only `cabinet_id` selects the cabinet. An empty `note` removes the note.

**Position.** When the request has only `latitude` or only `longitude`, SmartOLT pairs it with the stored other coordinate. SmartOLT removes the position when the resulting pair has an empty coordinate or is 0, 0.

**Zone change.** When the request moves the cabinet to another zone without a new `name`, the current name must be unique in the new zone.

SmartOLT removes the spaces at the start and the end of `name`, `external_id` and `note`. It saves at most 500 characters of `name` and 2000 characters of `note`, and cuts a longer value.

SmartOLT checks the zone only when the request has `zone`, and the other fields only when the request has them.

SmartOLT checks the request in this order and stops at the first refusal. A refused request changes nothing. The refusals are:

- the API key is read-only: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `Readonly API Key doesn't have rights to make changes.`
- the URL has no external ID and the request has no `cabinet_id`: HTTP 400, `error_code` `specify_cabinet_id`, message `Invalid parameters: Please specify the cabinet external ID or the cabinet_id`.
- no distribution cabinet has this external ID or this `cabinet_id`: HTTP 400, `error_code` `cabinet_does_not_exist`, message `Invalid parameters: Distribution cabinet does not exist`.
- the distribution cabinet is in a zone that is not in the data access group of the API key: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `The API key does not have access to this cabinet`.
- `zone` contains a character other than a letter (a-z, A-Z), a digit, a space, an underscore, a dot or a dash: HTTP 400, `error_code` `incorrect_zone`, message `Invalid parameters: The zone can contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces, underscore, dot and the dash (-) character`.
- `zone` names a zone that is not in the data access group of the API key: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `The API key does not have access to this zone`.
- `zone` matches no zone name: HTTP 400, `error_code` `zone_does_not_exist`, message `Invalid parameters: Zone does not exist`. SmartOLT does not create the zone.
- `zone` is empty, the API key has a data access group, and the group has two or more zones: HTTP 400, `error_code` `specify_zone`, message `Invalid parameters: Please specify a zone`.
- `name` is empty or contains only spaces: HTTP 400, `error_code` `specify_cabinet_name`, message `Invalid parameters: Please specify a name for the cabinet`.
- another distribution cabinet in the same zone has the same name: HTTP 400, `error_code` `cabinet_already_exists`, message `Invalid parameters: A cabinet with the same name already exists on this zone`. The comparison ignores letter case. When the cabinet has no zone, the name must be unique among the distribution cabinets that have no zone.
- `latitude` is not empty and is not a number greater than -90 and less than 90: HTTP 400, `error_code` `incorrect_latitude`, message `Invalid parameters: The Latitude is invalid`.
- `longitude` is not empty and is not a number from -180 to 180: HTTP 400, `error_code` `incorrect_longitude`, message `Invalid parameters: The Longitude is invalid`.
- `external_id` is longer than 191 characters: HTTP 400, `error_code` `incorrect_external_id`, message `Invalid parameters: The external ID is too long (maximum 191 characters)`.
- another distribution cabinet already has this `external_id`: HTTP 400, `error_code` `external_id_not_unique`, message `Invalid parameters: The external ID <external_id> is already used by another cabinet`. The comparison ignores letter case and trailing spaces.
- the request has none of `zone`, `name`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `external_id` and `note`: HTTP 400, `error_code` `nothing_to_update`, message `Invalid parameters: No fields to update were provided`.
- the database does not save the change: HTTP 500, `error_code` `cabinet_update_failed`, message `Could not update the cabinet`.

response.name: 200 - OK
400 - Cabinet does not exist
400 - Nothing to update
400 - External ID already used
403 - Read-only API key
403 - No access to the cabinet

item.name: Delete Distribution cabinet by unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

urlencoded.description: (Int) Internal numeric ID, as returned by Get Distribution cabinets list. When sent, it takes precedence over the external ID in the URL segment.

request.description:
Deletes a distribution cabinet.

**Selecting the distribution cabinet.** The URL segment is the unique `external_id` of the cabinet. The match ignores letter case. You can also post `cabinet_id` with the internal numeric ID. When the request has both, SmartOLT uses `cabinet_id`.

**What the delete changes.** SmartOLT deletes the cabinet in one transaction with these changes:

- the splitters that are directly in the cabinet leave it. They keep their position on the map;
- the ODFs and splitter boxes in the cabinet leave it. The splitters in those splitter boxes stay in their boxes;
- the splices and splice flips at the cabinet are deleted;
- the fiber routes that pass through the cabinet no longer pass through it. The routes stay.

SmartOLT checks the request in this order and stops at the first refusal. A refused request deletes nothing and changes nothing. The refusals are:

- the API key is read-only: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `Readonly API Key doesn't have rights to make changes.`
- the URL has no external ID and the request has no `cabinet_id`: HTTP 400, `error_code` `specify_cabinet_id`, message `Invalid parameters: Please specify the cabinet external ID or the cabinet_id`.
- no distribution cabinet has this external ID or this `cabinet_id`: HTTP 400, `error_code` `cabinet_does_not_exist`, message `Invalid parameters: Distribution cabinet does not exist`.
- the distribution cabinet is in a zone that is not in the data access group of the API key: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `The API key does not have access to this cabinet`.
- a fiber route starts or ends at the cabinet: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `This cabinet is connected to a fiber route and cannot be deleted`.
- sector restrictions are on in SmartOLT, the data access group of the API key has sectors, and a splitter directly in the cabinet has none of these sectors: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `This cabinet houses <count> ODB(s) and cannot be deleted`. `<count>` is the number of all splitters directly in the cabinet.
- another change holds the cabinet and SmartOLT cannot lock it: HTTP 400, `error_code` `cabinet_delete_failed`, message `Invalid parameters: Another change was using the cabinet at the same time, so the cabinet was not deleted. Try again.`
- another request deleted the cabinet after the first checks: HTTP 400, `error_code` `cabinet_does_not_exist`, message `Invalid parameters: Distribution cabinet does not exist. Nothing was deleted`.
- a fiber route started or ended at the cabinet while SmartOLT checked it: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `This cabinet is connected to a fiber route and cannot be deleted`.
- a fiber reserve is recorded at the cabinet: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `A fiber reserve is recorded at this cabinet. Delete the reserve first; the cabinet was not deleted`.
- a splice still uses a splitter of the cabinet: HTTP 403, `error_code` `forbidden`, message `A splitter in this cabinet still has splices. Delete those splices first`. This covers a splice in the cabinet that uses a splitter directly in the cabinet, a splice at a splitter box in the cabinet, and a splice at, or with, a splitter in such a box.
- the database does not save the delete: HTTP 400, `error_code` `cabinet_delete_failed`, message `Invalid parameters: The deleting of the cabinet failed`.

On success, `response` is `Distribution cabinet <name> deleted successfully`.

response.name: 200 - OK
400 - Cabinet does not exist
400 - Cabinet used by another change
403 - Read-only API key
403 - Connected to a fiber route
403 - Fiber reserve at the cabinet
403 - Splitters outside the sectors of the API key
403 - Splitter with splices

(String) ONU signal: Allowed values: very_good, warning, critical.
(String)ONU authorized on/after this date.
(String) ONU authorized on/before this date.

(String) Returns only the ONUs whose status changed at or after this date. Use ISO 8601 with a time zone, for example 2026-09-29T10:00:00+00:00. A date without a time zone is read in the time zone of your SmartOLT account.

request.description:
Gets all the ONUs details for a specified OLT ID, board, PON port or zone. If no OLT ID, board, PON port or zone is specified, then all the ONUs details on all OLTs will be returned.

The "Get all ONUs details" method is equivalent to an export of the entire database of ONU details and therefore it is not recommended to be used repeatedly, as the contained information does not change so often.

Maximum recommended calls for "Get all ONUs details": 15 per hour (calls are blocked after the limit is reached).

**Pagination (recommended)**

Pass `page` to receive results in pages. `page_size` accepts 1-100 (default 100). Paginated calls do **not** consume the 15/hours budget of the full export - they count toward the general API budget.

The paginated response is:

`{ "status": true, "page": 1, "page_size": 100, "total_items": 4111, "total_pages": 42, "onus": [...] }`

`total_items`/`total_pages` are included on page 1.

#### Keeping in sync (recommended pattern)

Page through the full inventory once, store it, then poll with `updated_since=` (e.g. `2026-07-08 12:00:00`) to receive only ONUs whose configuration changed since. A typical incremental sync is 1–2 calls instead of re-paging everything. Status/signal changes do not touch `updated_since` — use the dedicated statuses/signals endpoints for those.

#### Fields

- `seal_number`: the seal number of the ONU's drop cable at the splitter port, as text. It is `null` when the ONU has no seal number. Several ONUs can have the same seal number. It is returned with `fields=seal_number`.
- `wifi_ports[].ssid`: the SSID set in SmartOLT; when none is set, the SSID the ONU last reported.
- `wifi_ports[].reported_ssid`: the SSID the ONU last reported over TR-069.
- `wifi_ports[].ssid_reported_at`: when `reported_ssid` was read. Both are `null` when the ONU reported nothing.

#### Filters

All optional and combinable — see the query parameters table. Text filters (`sn`, `external_id`, `name`, `address`) match partially; enum filters return 400 on invalid values.

#### Full export

Calling without `page` returns every ONU in one response (`{ "status": true, "onus": [...] }`). This is equivalent to an export of the entire database: maximum 15 calls per hour, blocked at the limit. Prefer pagination + `updated_since`.

#### Errors

- 400 — unknown OLT ID / zone / splitter, board/port without the required OLT ID, or an invalid filter value (unparseable date, unknown status token)
- Unsupported query parameters are deprecated: they currently return a `Deprecation` warning header and will be rejected with 410 Gone
- 429 — rate limit exceeded; the response carries `Retry-After` (seconds until the counting window resets). Back off and retry after that interval

header.description: (Required) The API token

query.description: (Int) The ID of the OLT for which to get the ONUs GPS coordinates. Leave empty if you want ONUs GPS coordinates from all OLTs
(Int) OLT board where the ONUs are placed. Leave it empty if you want ONUs GPS coordinates from all boards on the provided OLT ID
(Int) OLT PON port where ONUs are placed. Leave it empty if you want ONUs GPS coordinates from all PON ports on the provided board

(String) The zone where the ONUs are located. The Zone can contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces, underscore and the dash (-) character. Leave it empty if you want ONUs GPS coordinates from all the zones

request.description:
Gets all the ONUs GPS coordinates for a specified OLT ID, board, PON port or zone. If no OLT ID, board, PON port or zone is specified, then all the ONUs GPS coordinates on all OLTs will be returned. Maximum recommended calls for "Get all ONUs GPS coordinates": 3 per hour (calls are blocked after the limit is reached). The response consists of:

  • ONU latitude

  • ONU longitude

It returns a 400 error code when:

  • no OLT was found for the provided OLT ID

  • no OLT ID was provided with board or PON port

  • no OLT ID or no board was provided with PON port

  • no Zone was found for the provided zone name

request.description:

Gets the ONU status for a specified ONU unique external ID. ONU status returned can be:
  • Online

  • OLT wasn't able to process the command
  • ONU is saved for later authorization and doesn't have a status yet

item.name: Get ONU status history by ONU unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

query.description: (String) The first day, as YYYY-MM-DD. Send it together with to. Leave both empty to get the last 24 hours.
(String) The last day, as YYYY-MM-DD. This day is included. It cannot be in the future.

request.description:
Gets the status history of an ONU for a time period: how long the ONU was Online, LOS, Power fail, Offline or Log in, and how many times it went down.

The data comes from the SmartOLT database. This endpoint does not send commands to the OLT.

Time period

  • Leave from and to empty to get the last 24 hours.
  • Or send from and to together, as YYYY-MM-DD. Both days are included. from can be up to 365 days ago.
  • All times are in the time zone of your SmartOLT account. The response shows it in timezone.

Detail

  • If the period starts in the last 7 days, detail is transitions. You get each status period in periods.
  • If the period starts earlier, detail is daily. You get the seconds in each status per day in days.

Fields

  • summary.online_percent: the percentage of time Online. Time with no data (unknown) is not counted. It is null when there is no data.
  • summary.seconds and days[].seconds: seconds in each status: online, los, power_fail, offline, login, unknown.
  • interruptions: how many times the ONU went from Online to another status.

item.name: Get ONU router hosts by ONU unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

request.description:
Returns the list of LAN hosts (connected devices) currently seen by the ONU's router, read live from the CPE over TR-069.

📡 Performs real-time data collection directly from the OLT  
**🔧 Designed for LIVE debugging and troubleshooting only**

**🚫 DO NOT call this endpoint every time your CRM loads a page**

❗ **Restrictions**🚫 DO NOT use this endpoint in:

- automated polling scripts
- monitoring loops
- bulk data collection jobs

**🚫 DO NOT call this endpoint repeatedly for multiple ONUs**

Use get_onu_router_hosts only when:

- actively debugging a specific ONU
- investigating a real-time issue reported by a user

**Only one call at a time:** This endpoint allows a single in-flight request at once. If another call to it is already being processed, further calls return HTTP 429 with `error_code: already_a_request_in_progress` — wait for the running call to finish before retrying.

The ONU must be online and TR-069 must be enabled and integrated on it; otherwise the device is treated as offline and the call fails.

**Success response** (`status: true`) contains `response.hostlist`, an object keyed by host index. Each host is the raw TR-069 `Hosts.Host` entry (fields such as `HostName`, `IPAddress`, `MACAddress`, `Active`, `AddressSource`, `Layer2Interface`, ...); available fields depend on the CPE.

Each host also has `wifi_signal_dbm`: the WiFi signal of that device in dBm (for example `-61`), read from the ONU's WiFi interfaces during the same call. It is `null` for a device connected by cable, for a WiFi device whose signal the ONU does not report, and when the ONU does not answer the WiFi read. The host list is returned in all three cases.

**Error codes** (`error_code` in the `{status:false, error, error_code}` body):

- `specify_field` (400) — no `onu_external_id` supplied.
- `specify_valid_field` (400) — no ONU matches the supplied id.
- `already_a_request_in_progress` (429) — another call to this endpoint is already running; retry after it completes.
- `tr069_unable_to_process_command` (400) — TR-069 not enabled/integrated on the ONU, or the device is offline / did not respond.
- `forbidden` (403) — id is outside your restriction group, or the OLT subscription is not valid.

item.name: Get ONU MAC addresses by ONU unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

request.description:
Gets the MAC addresses that the OLT learned behind one ONU, for a specified ONU unique external ID.

📡 This endpoint reads the data directly from the OLT. A call can take up to 2 minutes. Set the timeout of your HTTP client to at least 2 minutes. Use it for one ONU at a time.

Each MAC address has 12 lowercase hexadecimal characters with no separators, for example `a4b1c2d3e4f5`.

The response has `verified: true` only when the OLT answered. An empty `mac_addresses` list then means that the ONU has no MAC addresses. If the OLT did not answer, you get an error, not an empty list.

`source` says where the list comes from:

- `fdb`: the MAC addresses that the OLT learned behind the ONU, from the forwarding table of the OLT.
- `wan`: the MAC addresses of the WAN interfaces of the ONU itself, as the ONU reports them. SmartOLT reads them when the OLT forwarding table returns no MAC address for the ONU. Devices behind the ONU are not in this list.

The `wan` read works for GPON ONUs on Huawei OLTs and on ZTE C6xx OLTs.

`mac_details` gives the VLAN of each MAC address. On Huawei OLTs each element also has `gem_port`, and on ZTE OLTs it has `vport`, when the OLT reports one. A MAC address learned on two VLANs has two elements.

`mac_details` is optional. It is missing when the OLT did not give a VLAN for every MAC address. `mac_addresses` and `total` are always in the response.

It returns a 400 error code when:

- no ONU was found for the provided ONU external ID
- the OLT is unreachable (error code `olt_unreachable`)
- the OLT model does not support this read (error code `olt_script_not_available`)
- the OLT did not accept the command (error code `olt_unable_to_process_command`)

item.name: Search ONU by MAC address

header.description: (Required) The API token

query.description: (Required, String) The MAC address to find. You can use :, - or . as separators, or no separators.
(Int) The ID of the OLT to search. Leave it empty to search all OLTs. A search of all OLTs is slower and has a lower limit.

request.description:
Finds the ONU behind which the OLT learned a MAC address. This endpoint reads the data directly from the OLTs.

Limits (for your SmartOLT account, not for each API key):

  • With olt_id: one search every 10 seconds, and up to 100 searches per hour.
  • Without olt_id (all OLTs): one search every 60 seconds, and up to 10 searches per hour. The search can take up to about 4 minutes.
  • Only one search of each type can run at a time.
  • When you are over a limit, you get HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

How to read the result

  • verified is true only when all searched OLTs answered. If it is false and matches is empty, the MAC address can still be on an OLT that did not answer.
  • olts shows the result for each OLT: answered, skipped_unreachable, deadline, vendor_not_supported, subscription_expired or another failure.
  • matched_in_smartolt is false when the OLT has the MAC address on an ONU that is not in SmartOLT.
  • restricted is true when your API key cannot see that ONU. The ONU position is then null.

Only Huawei, ZTE and FiberHome OLTs are supported.

It returns a 400 error code when:

  • no MAC address was provided (error code specify_mac_address)
  • the MAC address is not valid (error code specify_valid_mac_address)
  • the OLT vendor is not supported (error code olt_vendor_not_supported)
  • the OLT with the provided olt_id did not answer (error code olt_unreachable)

header.description: (Required) The API token

request.description:
Returns all ONU authorization presets for a specified OLT unique ID.

## What the response tells you

`criteria` is what the preset matches on. `applies` is what it will configure:

- Names, not ids, for zone / splitter / ONU type / speed profiles / template.
    
- `odb_port_mode` — `null` if the preset sets no splitter, `"none"` if it attaches the ONU to the  
    splitter **without** a port, `"auto"` if a free port is picked at authorization time. A preset in  
    `auto` mode rejects a caller-supplied `odb_port`; one in `none` mode accepts it.
    
- `sets_tr069`, `sets_wifi`, `sets_wan`, `sets_web_credentials`, `sets_mgmt_ip` — booleans  
    only. The underlying credentials, WiFi config and PPPoE password are **never** selected by  
    this query, so they cannot leak through this endpoint. Each flag mirrors the condition the  
    matching apply step actually uses, so a `true` means the step will really run.
    

Presets are filtered by the API key's zone and VLAN restrictions: one pointing at a zone or  
VLAN outside your scope is dropped rather than disclosing its name or id.

item.name: Get all ONU authorization presets applicable to a specific ONU SN

header.description: (Required) The API token

query.description: (Required) OLT ID
(String) SN of the ONU you intend to authorize.
(Int) OLT board where the ONU is placed.
(Int) OLT PON port where ONU is placed.
(Optional, String) gpon | epon
(Optional, String) ONU type name

request.description:
Returns all ONU authorization presets for a specified OLT unique ID applicable to a specified ONU SN.

## Applicability

Send **any** of `sn`, `board`, `port` and the response also scores each preset against that  
ONU. Each preset then gains:

- `matches` — the same accept/reject verdict `authorize_onu` will apply
    
- `match_score` — how specific the match is (`null` when `matches` is false)
    

and the response gains `best_match_preset_id` — the preset that would win.

Omit all three and those three fields are **absent entirely**, rather than guessed. Test for  
their presence rather than for a falsy value.

Scoring: SN pattern `+200`; board **and** port `+100`; board or port alone `+50`; neither `+1`;  
pon_type `+10`; ONU type `+5`. Ties break on the default preset, then the lowest id.

`board` and `port` must be non-negative integers; anything else is rejected with  
`incorrect_field_value` rather than silently scoring against a different subject.

## What the response tells you

`criteria` is what the preset matches on. `applies` is what it will configure:

- Names, not ids, for zone / splitter / ONU type / speed profiles / template.
    
- `odb_port_mode` — `null` if the preset sets no splitter, `"none"` if it attaches the ONU to the  
    splitter **without** a port, `"auto"` if a free port is picked at authorization time. A preset in  
    `auto` mode rejects a caller-supplied `odb_port`; one in `none` mode accepts it.
    
- `sets_tr069`, `sets_wifi`, `sets_wan`, `sets_web_credentials`, `sets_mgmt_ip` — booleans  
    only. The underlying credentials, WiFi config and PPPoE password are **never** selected by  
    this query, so they cannot leak through this endpoint. Each flag mirrors the condition the  
    matching apply step actually uses, so a `true` means the step will really run.
    

Presets are filtered by the API key's zone and VLAN restrictions: one pointing at a zone or  
VLAN outside your scope is dropped rather than disclosing its name or id.

Call this with the SN, board and port from the unconfigured list, take  
`best_match_preset_id`, and pass it to `authorize_onu`.

Check `applies` on the chosen preset before building the authorize request — every field  
listed there must be **omitted** from your call, or it comes back as  
`authorization_preset_conflicting_parameter`.

request.description:
Authorizes an ONU using an authorization preset.

Identify the preset by `authorization_preset_id` (preferred) or `authorization_preset_name`.  
Send both and they must agree — names are compared case-insensitively, and a duplicated name  
returns `ambiguous_authorization_preset_name`.

`olt_id`, `pon_type` and `sn` are always required. `pon_type` is validated **before** the  
preset is resolved, so an invalid one reports `incorrect_pon_type` even if the preset id is  
also wrong.

## Online vs offline

Send `board` and `port` and the ONU is configured on the OLT immediately (**online**) — expect  
this call to take tens of seconds. Omit them and the ONU is recorded for configuration when it  
appears (**offline**).

> A preset carrying TR-069, management-IP or web-credential settings only applies those fully  
on the **online** path — they need a provisioned ONU. An offline call still returns success  
while applying just the parts that do not require one. WiFi and WAN settings are stored  
either way. 
  

## Fields the preset leaves open

Anything the preset does not set may be supplied and is validated normally — typically  
`name`, `address_or_comment`, `contact`, `onu_external_id`, `latitude`, `longitude`, and any of  
`vlan` / `cvlan` / `svlan` / `zone` / `odb` / `odb_port` / speed profiles / `custom_profile` /  
`onu_type` the preset happens to leave open.

If the preset auto-detects the ONU type, supply `onu_type` — your value wins over the preset's  
fallback type. With neither, the call fails with `specify_onu_type`.

## Preset zones are access-checked

A preset that would place the ONU into a zone (or onto an splitter in a zone) outside a restricted  
key's scope is refused with `403` / `forbidden`, exactly as a caller-supplied `zone` would be.

(String) Line-profile GEM mapping of the ONU. Allowed values: `prio`, `vlan`. `prio` maps the ONU traffic to GEM ports by priority. `vlan` maps the ONU traffic to GEM ports by VLAN (VLAN mapping). The parameter applies only when all these conditions are true:

request.description:
## Update ONU type for a specified ONU unique external ID

The request returns succesfully if the ONU type was changed successfully.

It returns a 400 error code when:

- no ONU external ID was provided
- no ONU was found for the provided ONU external ID
- no new ONU type was provided
- no ONU type was found with the given ONU type name
- the ONU type PON type is not compatible with the ONU
- `line_profile_maptype` is `vlan`, the ONU uses priority mapping and the ONU has more than 8 VLANs (`maximum_vlans_per_onu`)
- OLT was unable to process the command

### Line-profile mapping

When `line_profile_maptype` applies, the success response depends on the ONU type:

- With the current ONU type, the response is `Line profile mapping changed for ONU with ONU external ID <id>`.
- With a new ONU type, the response is `ONU type and line profile mapping changed for ONU with ONU external ID <id>`.

If the OLT does not accept the change, the request fails with `400` and `olt_unable_to_process_command`:

- When only the mapping changes, SmartOLT restores the previous mapping of the ONU.
- When the ONU type and the mapping change, SmartOLT restores the previous ONU type and the previous mapping.

If another request changes this ONU at the same time, the request returns HTTP 409 with `error_code` `onu_busy`, and SmartOLT does not change the ONU. Send the request again later.

item.name: Get ONU configuration presets

header.description: (Required) The API token

request.description:
List **every** configuration preset the API key can see.

Presets are returned in OLT-then-name order. Only presets belonging to OLTs the key has access to are included. Deleted presets, and presets whose OLT has been deleted, are never returned.

A configuration preset is a reusable set of ONU settings defined per OLT (optionally narrowed to a board/port). Applying a preset writes those settings to the ONU and pushes them to the OLT. A preset marked as _reversible_ records what it changed, so it can later be removed and the previous values restored. A non-reversible (one-time) preset is applied once and previous values cannot be restored.

**Optional query parameter**

- `olt_id` — return only the presets belonging to that OLT.
    

**Fields**

- `board` / `port` — `null` when the preset applies to the whole OLT, otherwise the board/port it is narrowed to.
    
- `is_reversible` — reversible presets can be removed later (`remove_configuration_preset`) and are reported in `applied_configuration_preset`. One-time presets apply their settings and keep no record.
    
- `enforced_settings` — the setting groups this preset governs, each as `{key, rows}` in a canonical order (e.g. `main_vlan`, `catv`, `tr069`). `rows` are RESOLVED display lines — `{label, value}` with IDs turned into names (VLAN, speed profile, TR-069 profile). A group can expand to several rows (e.g. `tr069` → mode, profile, interface). Secrets (WiFi/PPPoE/web passwords) are never read or returned.

response.name: 200 - OK

item.name: Apply configuration preset to an ONU by ONU unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

urlencoded.description: Required if configuration_preset_id is not sent. Name of an applicable preset.
Required if configuration_preset_name is not sent. ID of an applicable preset.

request.description:
Applies a configuration preset to the ONU and pushes the resulting configuration to the OLT.

Runs **synchronously** and returns the final outcome. If the OLT push fails, the preset application is rolled back automatically and the error is returned.

Identify the preset by `configuration_preset_id` **or** `configuration_preset_name` (at least one required). If you send both and they point at different presets the request is rejected with`configuration_preset_id_name_mismatch`.

The preset is always resolved against the presets applicable to this ONU, so a preset belonging to a different OLT/board/port is rejected with `configuration_preset_not_applicable`.

### Path parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onu_external_id` | yes | The ONU external ID |

### Body parameters (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`)

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `configuration_preset_id` | one of the two | ID of an applicable preset |
| `configuration_preset_name` | one of the two | Name of an applicable preset |

### Errors

`configuration_preset_id_or_name_required`, `configuration_preset_not_applicable`, `configuration_preset_id_name_mismatch, onu_busy` (409), plus any OLT error returned while pushing the configuration.

response.name: 200 - OK
400 - Preset not applicable to this ONU
409 - ONU busy

header.description: (Required) The API token

request.description:
Removes the configuration preset currently applied to the ONU, restoring the settings that were in place before it was applied, and pushes the result to the OLT.

Runs **synchronously** and returns the final outcome.

There is no preset parameter: the endpoint operates on whichever preset is currently applied on the ONU. If the ONU has no applied preset — or the applied preset was a **one-time (non-reversible)** preset, which by definition cannot be undone — the call returns `preset_application_not_found`.

### Path parameters

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `onu_external_id` | yes | The ONU external ID |

### Errors

`preset_application_not_found`, `onu_busy` (409), plus any OLT error returned while pushing the configuration.

400- Nothing to remove

request.description:
Applies a configuration preset to several ONUs in one call.

**This endpoint is asynchronous.** It validates each ONU, queues the work as a batch action and returns immediately — the response tells you what was _accepted_, not what the OLT did.

The response is a list keyed by ONU external id. Accepted ONUs report that the action is being processed; every other ONU carries the reason it was skipped. Duplicate ids in one call are collapsed, and an ONU that already has this action queued is not queued twice.

Per-ONU skip reasons include: preset not applicable to that ONU, the ONU already has a preset applied, and an action already queued for it.

| `configuration_preset_id` | one of the two | ID of the preset to apply |
| `configuration_preset_name` | one of the two | Name of the preset to apply — resolved per ONU |

header.description: (Required) The API token

urlencoded.description: (Required, String) Comma separated list of ONU unique external IDs. A maximum of 10 000 ONU unique external IDs are allowed

request.description:
Check how the queued configuration-preset work is going, detailed per ONU.

Reports the **most recent** preset task row for each ONU — apply or remove, whichever happened last — so it answers both "is my bulk request still running" and "what happened to it".

**`status`** **values**

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | accepted, not picked up by a worker yet |
| `in_progress` | a worker is running it now |
| `retrying` | an attempt failed; more attempts remain (up to 4) |
| `failed` | out of attempts, or the batch action was stopped, or its task is no longer running |
| `succeeded` | completed successfully |
| `no_task` | the ONU exists but has no preset task on record |
| `onu_not_found` | no ONU with that external id is visible to this API key |

**Other fields** (absent for `no_task` / `onu_not_found`)

- `action` — `apply` or `remove`.
    
- `attempts` — attempts made so far.
    
- `date_start` / `date_end` — `null` until the worker starts / finishes an attempt.
    
- `error_message` — the error from the last failed attempt, passed through from the OLT where there was one. Always `null` for `succeeded`.

response.name: 200 - OK

originalRequest.description:
How the queued configuration-preset work is going, per ONU.

Reports the **most recent** preset task row for each ONU — apply or remove, whichever happened last — so it answers both "is my bulk request still running" and "what happened to it". You do not need to hold a task id.

Costs the same two queries whether you ask about 1 ONU or 10000; the response grows with the number of ids, not the work behind them. Accepts up to 10000 ONU external ids, works with a read-only API key, and is exempt from the concurrent-call limit that applies to the mutating endpoints — you can poll it as often as you need.

**`status` values**

| value | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `queued` | accepted, not picked up by a worker yet |
| `in_progress` | a worker is running it now |
| `retrying` | an attempt failed; more attempts remain (up to 4) |
| `failed` | out of attempts, or the batch action was stopped, or its task is no longer running |
| `succeeded` | completed successfully |
| `no_task` | the ONU exists but has no preset task on record |
| `onu_not_found` | no ONU with that external id is visible to this API key |

**Other fields** (absent for `no_task` / `onu_not_found`)

- `action` — `apply` or `remove`.
- `attempts` — attempts made so far.
- `date_start` / `date_end` — `null` until the worker starts / finishes an attempt.
- `error_message` — the error from the last failed attempt, passed through from the OLT where there was one. Always `null` for `succeeded`.

item.name: Update ONU location details by ONU unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

formdata.description: (String) The zone where the ONU is located. The Zone can contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces, underscore and the dash (-) character
(String) Splitter. The Splitter can contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces, underscore and the dash (-) character

(Int) Splitter port. When odb_port is missing and the ONU stays on the same splitter, the ONU keeps its current splitter port. When odb is a different splitter and odb_port is missing, the ONU gets no splitter port.
(String) Name. The Name can contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces and the following characters: @#$&()-`.+,/_
(String) Address or comment. The Address or Comment can contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces and the following characters: @#$&()-`.+,/_
(String) Contact. The Contact can contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces and the following characters: @#$&()-`.+,/_
(String) Latitude
(String) Longitude

(String) Seal number of the ONU's drop cable at the splitter port. Up to 64 characters, without line breaks, other control characters or emoji. Spaces at the start and at the end are removed. Send `unknown` (any letter case) to remove the seal number. When the parameter is missing or empty, the seal number does not change. Several ONUs can have the same seal number. A request with only `seal_number` is valid. When the ONU moves to another splitter or splitter port, or leaves its splitter, SmartOLT removes its seal number, because the seal stays on the old drop cable. When the same request also sends `seal_number`, the ONU gets the value from the request.

request.description:
## Update ONU location details for a specified ONU unique external ID

At least one parameter must be provided. Send only the parameters that you want to be updated. The zone names must be the ones defined in SmartOLT Zones section. The Splitter names must be the ones defined in SmartOLT Splitters section.  
The request returns succesfully if the ONU location details were updated successfully.  
It returns a 400 error code when:

- no ONU external ID was provided
- no ONU was found for the provided ONU external ID
- no parameters were provided
- the Zone is in the wrong format
- the Splitter is in the wrong format
- the Name is in the wrong format
- the Address or Comment is in the wrong format
- the Contact is in the wrong format
- the Latitude is in the wrong format
- the Longitude is in the wrong format
- the Seal number is longer than 64 characters, or contains line breaks or other control characters (error code `incorrect_seal_number`)
- OLT was unable to process the command

When the seal number is not valid, the request fails before it changes anything: no location detail and no seal number is saved.

It returns a 500 error code when the seal number could not be saved (error code `internal_error`). The other location details of the same request may already be saved; send the request again.

item.name: Update ONU main VLAN-ID by ONU unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

formdata.description: (Required, Int) ONU new main VLAN-ID

request.description:
## Update ONU main VLAN-ID for a specified ONU unique external ID

The request returns succesfully if the ONU main VLAN-ID was updated successfully.

It returns a 400 error code when:

- no ONU external ID was provided
- no ONU was found for the provided ONU external ID
- no VLAN-ID was provided
- OLT was unable to process the command

### Imported ONUs that were not resynced

This section applies to an ONU that was imported from the OLT and was not resynced since. On such an ONU, the OLT still has the configuration that was imported. SmartOLT does not send the VLAN change on that configuration:

1. SmartOLT saves the new main VLAN-ID.
2. SmartOLT resyncs the ONU: it deletes the ONU from the OLT and configures it again with the settings saved in SmartOLT. The ONU is offline during the resync.
3. The success response is `Main VLAN-ID updated for ONU with ONU external ID <id>; the imported ONU was resynced`.

If SmartOLT cannot resync the ONU with the new VLAN-ID, the request fails with HTTP 400 and SmartOLT does not change the ONU:

- `not_supported_on_olt_model`: the OLT model does not support this configuration. The `error` text names the reason.
- `invalid_speed_profile`: a speed profile of the ONU cannot be sent to the OLT.
- `invalid_onu_type`: the ONU type name cannot be sent to the OLT.

If the resync fails after SmartOLT saved the new VLAN-ID, the request fails with HTTP 400 and `error_code` `main_vlan_saved_resync_needed`. The ONU stays marked for resync.

A request with the VLAN-ID that the ONU already has does not start a resync. When the ONU is still marked for resync after a failed resync, this request also fails with HTTP 400 and `main_vlan_saved_resync_needed`. Resync the ONU with `resync_config` to send the saved VLAN-ID to the OLT.

If another request changes this ONU at the same time, the request returns HTTP 409 with `error_code` `onu_busy`, and SmartOLT does not change the ONU. Send the request again later.

response.name: 200 - OK

item.name: Enable ONU DHCPv6 Option 18 by ONU unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

request.description:
## Enable DHCPv6 Option 18 for a specified ONU unique external ID

DHCPv6 Option 18 (Interface-ID) is the IPv6 counterpart of DHCP Option 82. The OLT adds the ONU port identification to the DHCPv6 requests of the ONU. The DHCPv6 server must accept Relay-Forward messages (RFC 6221).

It works on Huawei OLTs whose firmware supports it, on ZTE C300/C320 OLTs with firmware 2.x, and on ZTE C6xx OLTs. Some Huawei OLTs set DHCPv6 Option 18 for all their ONUs together, in the OLT advanced settings.

On success, the response has `status` `true`, and DHCPv6 Option 18 is enabled for the ONU.

It returns HTTP 400 when:

- no ONU was found for the provided ONU external ID;
- DHCPv6 Option 18 is not enabled in the OLT advanced settings (`error_code` `dhcpv6_option18_not_enabled_on_olt`);
- the OLT does not support DHCPv6 Option 18 (`error_code` `dhcpv6_option18_not_supported`);
- the OLT did not accept the command (`error_code` `olt_unable_to_process_command`).

In the first three cases SmartOLT sends no command to the OLT.

A read-only API key cannot use this call. The response is HTTP 403 with `error_code` `forbidden` and the message `Readonly API Key doesn't have rights to make changes.`, and SmartOLT does not change the ONU.

If another request changes this ONU at the same time, the request returns HTTP 409 with `error_code` `onu_busy`, and SmartOLT does not change the ONU. Send the request again later.

response.name: 200 - OK
400 - Option 18 not enabled for this OLT
403 - Forbidden

item.name: Update ONU speed profiles by ONU unique external ID

header.description: (Required) The API token

formdata.description: (String) Upload speed profile name
(String) Download speed profile name
(Integer) Send 1 to queue the work and return immediately. Send 0 or leave it out to run the work in the request. Default: 0

request.description:
Update ONU upload and download speed profiles for a specified ONU unique external ID

At least one speed profile name must be provided. The profile names must be the ones defined in SmartOLT Speed Profiles section. The request returns succesfully if the profile names on the ONU were updated or the profiles names provided are the same as the ones already saved on the ONU. It returns a 400 error code when:
  • no ONU external ID was provided
  • no ONU was found for the provided ONU external ID
  • no speed profile names were provided
  • no upload speed profile was found with the name provided
  • no download speed profile was found with the name provided
  • OLT was unable to process the command

Asynchronous mode (async=1)

Send async = 1 to queue the work and return immediately. SmartOLT first does the same checks as in the normal mode. If a check fails, the request returns the same 400 error.

If you do not send async, or you send 0, the request works as described above.

In asynchronous mode:

  • the response tells you that the action was accepted, not what the OLT did
  • the response contains "queued": true
  • if the newest queued action for this ONU is the same action, the ONU is not queued again
  • the action is queued also when the speed profiles are the same as the ones saved on the ONU
  • SmartOLT runs all actions for one ONU in the order it received them
  • OLT errors are not returned in this response. Use check_bulk_task_status to see the result
  • the call counts in the hourly budget for asynchronous calls, not in the normal hourly budget

ONU with queued actions

If the ONU already has queued actions, a request without async is also queued. This keeps the actions in the order SmartOLT received them. The response then contains "queued": true. Do not mark the action as done when you see this field. Use check_bulk_task_status to see the result.

If another request changes this ONU at the same time, the request returns error 409 with error_code onu_busy. Send the request again later.

Asynchronous mode (async=1)

Send async = 1 to queue the work and return immediately. SmartOLT first does the same checks as in the normal mode. If a check fails, the request returns the same 400 error.

If another request changes this ONU at the same time, the request returns error 409 with error_code onu_busy. Send the request again later.

item.name: Check bulk task status

header.description: (Required) The API token

urlencoded.description: (Required, String) Comma separated list of ONU unique external IDs. A maximum of 10 000 ONU unique external IDs are allowed

request.description:
Check how the work queued by the bulk endpoints with async=1 is going, detailed per ONU.

Reports the most recent enable, disable, speed profile or CATV task row for each ONU, whichever happened last, so it answers both "is my bulk request still running" and "what happened to it".

status values

| value | meaning | | --- | --- | | `queued` | accepted, not picked up by a worker yet | | `in_progress` | a worker is running it now | | `retrying` | an attempt failed; more attempts remain (up to 4) | | `failed` | out of attempts, or the batch action was stopped, or its task is no longer running | | `succeeded` | completed successfully | | `no_task` | the ONU exists but has no enable, disable, speed profile or CATV task on record | | `onu_not_found` | no ONU with that external id is visible to this API key |

Other fields (absent for no_task / onu_not_found)

  • action — enable, disable, update_speed_profiles, enable_catv or disable_catv. catv_sync means a CATV sync started from the SmartOLT web interface.
  • attempts — attempts made so far.
  • date_start / date_end — null until the worker starts / finishes an attempt.
  • error_message — the error from the last failed attempt, passed through from the OLT where there was one. Always null for succeeded.

The row can also come from an action that was not started by the API, for example a batch action in the SmartOLT web interface or the automatic sync.

Configuration preset tasks are not included. Use check_configuration_preset_task_status for them.

response.name: 200 - OK

item.name: Resolve an external ticket on an ONU

header.description: (Required) The API token

urlencoded.description: (Required) (String) The number of the ticket to resolve, as sent when the ticket was opened. When the ONU has no open external ticket with this number, the request returns HTTP 404 with `error_code` `not_found`.

request.description:
## Resolve an external ticket on an ONU

Resolves the open external ticket with this `ticket_number` on the ONU. SmartOLT sets its status to `solved` and records the change in the ticket history.

A read-only API key cannot use this call. The response is HTTP 403 with `error_code` `forbidden` and the message `Readonly API Key doesn't have rights to make changes.`, and SmartOLT does not change the ticket.

It returns HTTP 404 with `error_code` `not_found` when the ONU has no open external ticket with this number. A ticket with this number that is already resolved gives the same response. It returns HTTP 400 when no ONU was found for the provided ONU external ID. It returns HTTP 409 with `error_code` `ticket_changed` when another change to the ticket was saved at the same moment; the ticket stays open, so send the request again.

header.description: (Required) The API token

query.description: (Int) Page size when the ONU external ID is left out, 1 to 1000. Default 500. Another value returns HTTP 400 with `error_code` `invalid_paging`.
(Int) Number of tickets to skip when the ONU external ID is left out, 0 or more. Default 0. A negative value returns HTTP 400 with `error_code` `invalid_paging`.

request.description:
## Get open external tickets

Returns the open external tickets of one ONU, oldest first.

Leave out the ONU external ID to get one page of the open external tickets of every ONU that the API key can reach, oldest first. `limit` sets the page size, from 1 to 1000; the default is 500. `offset` sets how many tickets to skip, 0 or more; the default is 0. `has_more` is `true` when another page follows. The tickets in this list have no `note` field. The list leaves out the ONUs of OLTs with an expired subscription, and `expired_olts` lists those OLTs.

Responses include `assignee_email` only for an API key that is not read-only, has the **User management** option enabled and has no data access group. For any other key the field is omitted; `assignee_user_id` is always returned.

It returns HTTP 400 when no ONU was found for the provided ONU external ID. It returns HTTP 400 with `error_code` `invalid_paging` when `limit` is not from 1 to 1000, or when `offset` is less than 0.
